entry.summary: Visa-free short stays as part of the Schengen area.
entry.max_stay: 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area
entry.pre_arrival: None today. ETIAS is on the watch list.
entry.other: Schengen Entry/Exit System: fingerprints and photo at the border on first entry (free, nothing to do beforehand). Get an entry stamp where one is still given, and carry your passport across internal borders.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The currency in Slovenia is the Euro (EUR). Declare more than 10,000 euros or equivalent funds if you're travelling between Slovenia and a non-EU country. This covers all forms of currency, not just cash. Failure to do so will result in fines. You don't need to declare cash if you're travelling to or from another EU country. ATMs may be rare in mountain areas or small villages.

consular.mission: Australian Consulate, Ljubljana; Australian Embassy, Vienna
consular.notes: Australia has a consulate in Ljubljana headed by an Honorary Consul. The office provides some consular assistance but can't issue emergency passports or perform notarial acts. Get in contact before you visit.

laws.rule: For specific information on bringing medication into Slovenia, read the Import of Medications website.
laws.heading: Medications

laws.rule: You can drive on your Australian driver's licence for up to 12 months after arrival. Some car hire agencies may need you to have an International Driving Permit (IDP). Get your IDP before you leave Australia.

tourism.detail: Visa-free short stays as part of the Schengen area.

meetings.detail: Business meetings are covered, without being employed in the country.

conference.detail: Business travel, including conferences, is covered.

unpaid-speaking.detail: Unpaid speaking during a business visit is generally covered; the paid-activity exclusion is read narrowly.
unpaid-speaking.next: If unsure, ask Embassy of the Republic of Slovenia, O'Malley.

paid-speaking.detail: Paid activity isn't covered by the visa-free stay; most member states need a national visa and work permit, even under 90 days. Ask the Embassy of the Republic of Slovenia, O'Malley.
paid-speaking.next: Paid activity isn't covered by the visa-free stay; most member states need a national visa and work permit, even under 90 days. Ask the Embassy of the Republic of Slovenia, O'Malley.

remote-work.detail: Remote work for an employer outside the EU isn't addressed in the EU guidance read.
remote-work.next: Ask the Embassy of the Republic of Slovenia, O'Malley.

entrepreneur.detail: Exploring and meeting fit a business visit; running a business needs national permission.
entrepreneur.next: Ask the Embassy of the Republic of Slovenia, O'Malley.

trade.detail: Business visits are covered; selling or delivering services may be paid activity.
trade.next: Keep the trip to meetings and negotiation.

artist.detail: Paid activity isn't covered by the visa-free stay; most member states need a national visa and work permit, even under 90 days. Ask the Embassy of the Republic of Slovenia, O'Malley.
artist.next: Paid activity isn't covered by the visa-free stay; most member states need a national visa and work permit, even under 90 days. Ask the Embassy of the Republic of Slovenia, O'Malley.

mixed-mission.detail: The visa-free stay covers the business and tourism parts; any paid part needs national permission.
mixed-mission.next: Ask the Embassy of the Republic of Slovenia, O'Malley.

filming.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (journalistic or media purposes)
filming.detail: Journalistic or media purposes are listed among visa-free purposes; paid production work and location permits are national matters.
filming.next: Ask the Embassy of the Republic of Slovenia, O'Malley about filming, and the local authority about locations.

research.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (short-term study or training)
research.detail: Short-term study and training are covered; paid research at an institution is paid activity.
research.next: Ask the Embassy of the Republic of Slovenia, O'Malley if the host pays you.

volunteering.detail: Volunteering isn't addressed in the EU guidance read.
volunteering.next: Ask the Embassy of the Republic of Slovenia, O'Malley.
